working_identification: OXI ONE; MKII is the documented reference here
manual_edition: HTML pages identify firmware 2.2.10 / manual v2.0a
scope: 15 original manual diagrams visually inspected; selected manual sections researched. No hands-on hardware test or engine source adoption.
licence_status: Commercial UX reference; reusable OXI ONE engine source/licence not established. Artwork remains local research material.

assets.title: Mono note entry
assets.observed: Pitch rows and time columns show one active pitch at each step, with scrolling instructions beside the grid.
assets.optisynth_inference: Reuse the note editor for mono entry, with a visible voice constraint and a reversible conversion to polyphonic content.

assets.title: Polyphonic note entry
assets.observed: The same axes now show several pitches per column; the diagram distinguishes the note starts and continuations.
assets.optisynth_inference: Share selection and duration editing with Mono. Voice limits must be explicit; do not silently delete earlier notes when a limit is exceeded.

assets.title: Multitrack grid and selection
assets.observed: Rows now mean tracks. The first column also selects a track; held Mute changes the edge columns into mute/solo controls.
assets.optisynth_inference: Use separate named track headers on desktop so selecting a track cannot accidentally add its first note.

assets.title: Chord sequence
assets.observed: Rows label scale-related chords with miniature keyboard voicings, while columns still represent musical time.
assets.optisynth_inference: A chord progression editor should retain chord identity and expose the resulting notes, rather than storing only a flattened piano roll.

assets.title: Chord palette
assets.observed: Three lower rows distinguish basic, extended and altered chord choices. A colour legend identifies qualities; modifier pads occupy a separate area.
assets.optisynth_inference: Provide an auditionable chord palette with explicit names and voiced-note previews. Keep colour supplementary to text and interval labels.

assets.title: Stochastic probability controls
assets.observed: Columns represent candidate notes and rows their probabilities. Four rightmost columns control octave range, division and pitch/rhythm randomisation.
assets.optisynth_inference: Label the axes by model. Display generated phrase history separately; a moving timeline cursor over this probability grid can mislead.

assets.title: Matriceal track and parameter layout
assets.observed: Four track regions each contain a step area, ten parameter selectors and a track status row.
assets.optisynth_inference: Retain independent lane sequencing but use named lane tabs, visible loop lengths and separate phase markers in the larger focus editor.

assets.title: Domino trigger and note layers
assets.observed: Note steps and trigger steps occupy separate regions with separately labelled cursors; a keyboard sits below.
assets.optisynth_inference: Show the causal link between the rhythm lane and note-advance lane. An Advance source selector must distinguish every clock from accepted triggers.

assets.title: Saga stages
assets.observed: Stages run across successive rows; active notes, configured length and current stage use different indications. The keyboard remains below.
assets.optisynth_inference: Use stage cards with explicit duration and elapsed sub-position. The equal-size pad layout should not imply equal elapsed time.

assets.title: Saga duration example
assets.observed: The example adds three ticks to a 32-stage sequence because one stage lasts four ticks; an offset diagram is shown separately.
assets.optisynth_inference: Display total cycle duration alongside stage count. Treat gate length, stage dwell and note timing offset as separate concepts.

assets.title: Arranger slots and states
assets.observed: The arranger labels instrument rows, section columns and distinct playing, queued, blank-spacer and unused cells.
assets.optisynth_inference: Show pending launches explicitly and distinguish an intentional silent slot from an unused slot. Make opening the arrangement and arming playback separate actions.

assets.title: Performance overview
assets.observed: Rows identify different sequencer models, and their control groupings differ within the shared performance grid.
assets.optisynth_inference: A performance dashboard can share placement while adapting available actions to each loaded model. Keep persistent performance mutes visible outside this page.

assets.title: Modulation values and output
assets.observed: The figure separates entered modulation values from resulting output after offset, with independent length/division controls.
assets.optisynth_inference: Keep base value, modulation and effective output inspectable. Use an explicit bipolar axis and destination units in the desktop editor.

assets.title: Harmonic leader and followers
assets.observed: A leader feeds harmonic information to a follower that retains its own rhythmic pattern. Keyboard and sequencer inputs are shown separately.
assets.optisynth_inference: Model harmonic following as an explicit relationship with an inspectable leader, scale/chord state and bypass; do not hide it inside a global transpose knob.

assets.title: Snapshot status
assets.observed: A camera symbol marks the snapshot state in the main status display.
assets.optisynth_inference: Provide a visible performance snapshot with restore and discard actions whose scope is clear. Distinguish it from ordinary edit undo and preset saving.
